entries.literalBodyMarkdown: Search for technological bottlenecks that vanish if a hypothetical material property exists, then search matter-space specifically for that property.
Find sets of observations that strongly suggest a deeper invariance not captured by current theory.
Search experimental anomalies for patterns consistent with genuinely incomplete physical models, while aggressively rejecting instrumentation error and statistical artifacts.
Ask whether physical laws themselves exhibit deeper regularities. Not inventing physics by fantasy, but searching for meta-structure across successful theories.

entries.literalTitle: THE THEORY GENERATOR OF THEORY GENERATORS
entries.literalBodyMarkdown: Instead of proposing theories, evolve architectures whose specialty is generating classes of theories.
Generate specialized AI scientist architectures optimized for different epistemic environments, rather than one universal science agent.
Construct invention processes tailored to the domain, constraints, maturity, data regime, and available experimental tools.
Compete the systems that create inventors, scientists, algorithms, institutions, and experiments. Selection moves one meta-level upward.
Don't evolve solutions. Evolve **ways of evolving solutions**.
Compete different scientific methods against one another on synthetic and real discovery environments.
Evolve formal systems according to their explanatory and computational usefulness.
Evolve architectures that decide which reasoning architectures should be created next.
Institutions evolve not only their policies but the mechanisms by which policies themselves evolve.
A civilization that explicitly optimizes its ability to redesign its own scientific, economic, educational, technological, and governance machinery.
Give civilization a continuously updated model of itself: capabilities, dependencies, ignorance, fragilities, resources, technologies, knowledge, and reachable futures.
When the model discovers a mismatch between what civilization believes it can do and what evidence shows, automatically surface the discrepancy and its consequences.
Explore alternative scientific priorities, infrastructure investments, educational systems, technological pathways, and institutional mechanisms before committing generations.
Measure not GDP or productivity alone but the number and quality of future civilization states that remain reachable.
Protect capabilities, knowledge, biodiversity, manufacturing skills, scientific expertise, and technologies whose disappearance would permanently close valuable future branches.
Systematically identify technological and institutional pathways that consume enormous resources while shrinking long-term possibility space.
Capital allocation incorporates the option value of technologies that unlock entire future technology trees, not merely expected near-term profit.
Allocate resources dynamically to experiments based on expected information gain × transformative branching potential × reproducibility.
Markets trade not just assets but contingent claims on technological pathways. Information about which futures are becoming feasible becomes economically legible.
Represent emerging technology trees and their dependencies so funding can target enabling nodes instead of fashionable endpoints.
Rank interventions by how many future capabilities they unlock rather than just direct output.
Reward inventions partly according to the number of valuable subsequent inventions they make possible.

Measure:
     \[
     \frac{d(\text{future discovery capacity})}{d(\text{new technology})}
     \]
     Technologies with enormous derivative values become strategic priorities.

Go further:
     \[
     \frac{d^2(\text{discovery capacity})}{dt^2}
     \]
     Optimize technologies that accelerate the rate at which the rate of invention grows.
Discover positive loops linking education, science, capital, computation, manufacturing, energy, and institutional quality, then deliberately strengthen them.
When different discoveries enter the system, automatically search for combinations whose joint consequences exceed the sum of the parts.
A discovery triggers search for its first-order applications, whose existence triggers second-order discoveries, continuing recursively until the tree is exhausted.
Humanity routinely underestimates consequences of major inventions. Simulate technological aftershocks decades deep and identify surprising descendant industries.
Build a graph showing which historical inventions made which later inventions possible. Learn the structural patterns preceding civilization-changing breakthroughs.
Generate hypothetical future invention family trees and search backward for the earliest root technology we can build now.
Don't judge a technology by what it does. Judge it by what its descendants could do.
Extend evaluation multiple generations. A boring primitive might hide behind it an extraordinary technological civilization.
Start from a fantastical future capability and infer what early primitive would have to be its ancestor.
Invent hypothetical artifacts from advanced civilizations and reconstruct the minimum technology tree required to produce them.
Populate a database of inventions that cannot yet be built but become feasible after specified dependencies are solved.
Preserve technically sound ideas whose enabling technology does not yet exist and automatically resurrect them when prerequisites arrive.
Revisit inventions that failed historically because they were premature. Some dead ideas become brilliant once materials, computation, or economics change.
Search abandoned research programs, extinct industries, forgotten patents, failed scientific theories, and unrealized infrastructure plans for branches civilization prematurely pruned.
Ask what industrial revolution could have happened instead of steam → electricity → electronics. Maybe other viable technological trees were historically missed.
Simulate worlds where key discoveries arrived in different orders and harvest technologies that emerge only under alternate sequences.
Some discoveries may be much more powerful if developed before others. Search for optimal sequencing of civilization's technology tree.
Decide which discoveries to pursue now because they maximize the speed of all downstream discovery.
Prioritize knowledge that increases the productivity of future knowledge acquisition. Knowledge becomes recursive capital.
Invest compute, education, experiments, and tools where each improvement increases the rate of acquiring the next improvement.
Prefer capabilities that unlock many other capabilities. Tool-making ability dominates isolated tools.
Prefer actions that increase the number of future actions available rather than consuming optionality.
Search for interventions that improve many unrelated systems because they touch a shared bottleneck: energy, trust, computation, measurement, cognition, manufacturing, or something unknown.
Determine which single missing capability most constrains civilization's next thousand advances.
Remove the current bottleneck, immediately identify the next emergent bottleneck, repeat.
Treat civilization as a vast adaptive system and estimate which interventions most steeply improve long-term reachable states.
Rather than minimizing problems, maximize emergence of new useful capability.
Estimate which direction in technology-space expands reachable possibility fastest.
Civilization receives an orientation system pointing not north, but toward regions of maximum unexplored constructive possibility.

entries.literalTitle: THE CIVILIZATION MAP OF THE UNKNOWN
entries.literalBodyMarkdown: A dynamic atlas where known sciences form continents and unexplained structures define coastlines leading into intellectual oceans.
Treat invention space geometrically. Identify dense clusters, bridges, isolated islands, unexplored basins, and high-dimensional shortcuts.
Discover surprising short paths between distant technological regions. A result in fungal biology might unexpectedly unlock spacecraft materials.
When two valuable regions of possibility cannot connect because one intermediate capability is missing, invent the bridge.
Search for technology families that are unreachable through obvious incremental improvement but accessible through a discontinuous conceptual jump.
Specifically hunt inventions whose value jumps discontinuously once one threshold is crossed: superconductivity, controlled fusion, general-purpose robotics, molecular manufacturing, etc.
Find systems where gradual investment suddenly triggers qualitatively new behavior and optimize for crossing those boundaries.
Map combinations of energy, computation, coordination, intelligence, manufacturing, and knowledge that create qualitatively different civilization regimes.
Identify civilization parameters that sit near critical points where tiny improvements unlock huge systemic transitions.
Search for tiny interventions capable of initiating enormous positive technological cascades.
The mission is to discover the next technological primitive whose existence makes a previously impossible world suddenly obvious.
Fire wasn't merely energy. It transformed food, materials, protection, culture, migration, and eventually industry. Search deliberately for technologies with similarly broad primitive leverage.
Writing externalized memory. Find the next technology that externalizes a fundamental cognitive function humanity currently keeps trapped inside individuals.
Search for something that reduces the replication cost of another valuable entity by many orders of magnitude.
Search for a mechanism that makes a previously scarce form of usable work abundant.
Search for a universal carrier analogous to electricity: easily generated, transmitted, transformed, and consumed across countless applications.
Search for a tiny, manufacturable primitive whose composition yields arbitrarily complex systems.
Search for something whose value grows explosively when heterogeneous entities become interoperably connected.
Search for another previously human-exclusive function that could become technologically scalable, just as AI scales cognition.
Explicitly search for the category that becomes possible only once intelligence itself becomes abundant.

entries.literalTitle: THE TECHNOLOGY AFTER THE TECHNOLOGY AFTER AI
entries.literalBodyMarkdown: Don't stop at the immediate successor. Model generations of post-AI primitives and work backward toward their present-day roots.
Ask what becomes scarce after cognition becomes cheap. Perhaps experiments, energy, trust, physical action, unique experiences, rights, attention, or something entirely new.
Every time technology eliminates one scarcity, predict the next binding constraint and attack it early.
Systematically remove major scarcity classes in an order where solving one makes solving the next cheaper.
Input a scarce capability. Output the technology tree necessary to make it abundant.
Cheap energy enables cheap computation. Cheap computation enables cheap intelligence. Cheap intelligence accelerates materials science. Better materials improve energy. Recursive abundance.
Search for loops where abundance in one domain creates abundance in another until multiple scarcity barriers collapse together.
Determine which constraints remain even if energy, intelligence, and manufacturing become extremely cheap.
If many goods become cheap, identify what humans actually value when material scarcity weakens: meaning, novelty, authenticity, relationships, status, experiences, agency, time.
Treat meaning not as a commodity to manufacture but as a phenomenon whose conditions can be scientifically understood, allowing environments that better support purpose and flourishing.
Build a rigorous multidimensional science of what makes lives genuinely worth living without collapsing human value into one simplistic metric.
Translate an individual's values and constraints into experimentally testable life architectures while preserving autonomy and uncertainty.
